clue.text: How to surprise a goalkeeper and win easily?

definitions.meaning: a shot struck from far out can catch a keeper off his line
to win by a huge margin, as in a race won by a wide distance

explanation.surface: A football tactic question: how to catch the keeper out and stroll to victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by a wide margin, and taken literally it is a strike from distance at goal.

clue.text: Two male animals bound for cover

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Two male beasts are heading off to shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two male animals' gives two pieces; 'bound for' is a link, saying they are destined to become the answer, though it also hints at bookbinding.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiffened cloth used to cover books in binding.

clue.text: It's socially acceptable in workers-relatively speaking

indicators.note: the letter for acceptability sits inside the word for workers

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers
U is the old label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage

explanation.surface: A remark that something is acceptable among the working class, in family terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link. U-and-non-U was a 1950s British classification of upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in terms of family relations, these are female relatives, sisters of a parent.

clue.text: With which one suffers a lack of balance

definitions.text: With which one suffers a lack of balance

parts.words: With which one suffers a lack of balance
parts.note: reads as a physical wobble, but balance here is money in a bank account

explanation.definitionFit: Overdrawing a bank account leaves a negative figure, so there is no credit left.

clue.text: Turns and leaves

definitions.meaning: ... as in turns taken in a game

explanation.definitionFit: A player's go is a turn, and to go is to depart.

clue.text: Injury when outside left fouled is a break

indicators.note: the word for injury is placed round the rest

parts.note: harm means damage or injury

indicators.note: fouled means messed up, so the letters of left are scrambled

explanation.surface: A football report: a foul on the outside-left caused an injury and a stoppage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link. The football surface makes 'outside left' look like a playing position, but 'outside' is the container signal and 'fouled' scrambles 'left' into LFTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mid-term school holiday is a short break from lessons.

clue.text: Instruct attendants

definitions.meaning: a retinue following a royal or noble person

explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to teach, and a retinue of followers is a royal's suite.

clue.text: He tries to catch someone out

definitions.text: He tries to catch someone out

parts.words: He tries to catch someone out
parts.note: sounds like a trickster or detective, but describes a cricket player catching a batsman

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the side not batting stand round the pitch hoping to take catches that dismiss a batsman.

clue.text: Local ranch where Incas ate perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A South American ranch where the Incas might have dined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is a link; 'perhaps' rearranges INCAS ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish-speaking South America, a large cattle farm is called this, so it is the local word for a ranch.

clue.text: Fish gone astray in the fisherman's basket

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit within the basket word

parts.note: a creel is an angler's wicker basket

indicators.note: gone astray means wandered off course, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fish has gone missing from the angler's basket.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishing surface makes 'gone astray' read as a lost catch; 'astray' scrambles 'gone' into ONGE, and 'in' sets it inside the basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea eel is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Beer is put in the passage

indicators.note: is placed inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has left beer in the corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats or shelves is a passage.

clue.text: Settle concerning interest

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a side is a party or faction, one interest in a dispute

explanation.surface: A business note about settling a matter of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle somewhere is to make one's home there, to dwell.

clue.text: Normal colours

definitions.meaning: a flag or banner, as regimental colours

explanation.definitionFit: The usual level is the norm, and a regiment's flag carried into battle is its colours.

clue.text: Officer assisting general in plan that's crazy

indicators.note: the officer's letters go inside the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
ADC is aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a senior commander

explanation.surface: A general's aide has come up with a lunatic scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildly reckless or eccentric scheme or person is called this.

clue.text: TV's pop group?

parts.note: pop as father, and a TV show about a group of older men

explanation.definitionFit: A classic BBC sitcom about the Home Guard, Britain's wartime volunteer force of older men, hence a band of fathers.

clue.text: One who makes it in the world of drama?

definitions.text: One who makes it in the world of drama?

parts.words: One who makes it in the world of drama?
parts.note: reads as someone successful in theatre, but means the person who puts a show on

explanation.definitionFit: The person who organises and finances a play or film literally makes it happen.

clue.text: Immoderate road speed of a reckless person

indicators.note: an immoderate road speed is wild, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: Excessive speed on the road marks out a reckless driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold outlaw ready to take wild risks is a reckless person.

clue.text: Political organisation essentially dynamic

definitions.meaning: a campaigning group, as a protest or labour group
dynamics is at heart the study of motion

explanation.definitionFit: A campaigning body is a political group, and motion is the essence of anything dynamic.

clue.text: Without it there would be total ignorance

definitions.text: Without it there would be total ignorance

parts.words: Without it there would be total ignorance
parts.note: total here is a sum, so without adding no one would know any total

explanation.definitionFit: Summing numbers is how a total is found, so without it no total could be known.

clue.text: Dire Straits are recording ones

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, so the letters are badly arranged

explanation.surface: The band Dire Straits are recording musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Dire Straits is a British rock band, so 'Dire' hides in plain sight as the anagram signal; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians who make records are recording artists, the people in question.

clue.text: Man is, whatever Donne says

parts.note: John Donne wrote that no man is one, but the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is one

explanation.definitionFit: Land surrounded by sea, which the Isle of Man is, despite Donne's famous line.

clue.text: Taken from jumble and worn

indicators.note: jumble means mix up, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Clothes taken from a jumble sale and worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumble' reads as a jumble sale, a British charity sale of second-hand goods, but rearranges AND WORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds or knowledge drawn on are taken from a source.

clue.text: Side to side movement in soccer, perhaps

definitions.text: Side to side movement in soccer, perhaps

parts.words: Side to side movement in soccer, perhaps
parts.note: reads as a sideways pass, but side means team, as a player moves between clubs

explanation.definitionFit: A footballer's move from one club to another is the deal that shifts him between teams.

clue.text: Prime Minister's gone up to rest

indicators.note: in a down clue, gone up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister has gone upstairs to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'gone up' turns PEELS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is the body's nightly rest.

clue.text: Game in which you have to leap about

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sport in which players must jump around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which you have' is a link; 'about' rearranges TO LEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A Basque ball sport played against a wall, also called jai alai.

clue.text: Rosie's willowy form

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun, a kind of willow

indicators.note: form means shape, so the name is re-formed into new letters

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Rosie has a slender, graceful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a species of willow used in basketry, so willowy points to it loosely.

clue.text: Jewish priest of evil disposition

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A priest with a wicked temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'disposition' reads as temperament but signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was the founder of the priestly tribe, and a Levite served in the Temple.

clue.text: Some thousand held captive in battle

indicators.note: the letter for a thousand is held within the other word

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Around a thousand soldiers were taken prisoner in a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A First World War offensive of 1916 in northern France, named after its river.

clue.text: The height of architectural draughtsmanship

definitions.meaning: a flat drawing of one face of a building

explanation.definitionFit: Altitude is height, and an architect's drawing of a building's face has the same name.

clue.text: What a man who intrudes in a row will do

definitions.text: What a man who intrudes in a row will do

parts.words: What a man who intrudes in a row will do
parts.note: row as a quarrel, and row as rowing a boat with a paddle

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to meddle, with a pun on rowing.
